hook.text: Researchers told elderly adults to take weekly 15-minute 'awe walks.' After 8 weeks, their joy scores soared.

buildup.text: An awe walk means deliberately noticing vastness: the sky, old trees, intricate architecture, or distant views.

discovery.text: Participants took selfies during walks. Over weeks, their faces grew smaller as landscapes filled the frame.

twist.text: Regular walkers without the awe instruction showed no emotional change. Attention to wonder is the key.

climax.text: Awe walks reduced daily stress more effectively than gratitude journaling in the same study.

punchline.text: Wonder is free. You just have to look up.

quiz.question: What changed in participants' selfies during awe walks?
options: Their faces grew smaller in the frame
